description: Editing commands (§6.5), pasting (§6.5.1), writable cells (§7.1) and reading typed text (§7.3).

cases.description: The editor starts with the cell's text form (§7.3) and keeps the cell's value.
Null starts as the empty string.
Cells of a view with aggregate are not written.
Capabilities without write offer no writes.
The write carries the context's revision, and previous is the editor's value.
A value that does not change is not written.
A string of only white space is null.
Strings keep the white space around them.
The active cell moves as advance moves it: Tab in a range walks through it.
Cells are written row by row; blank cells are left out.
The empty string is blank in a string column.
A write holds at most 100,000 cells.
Values go from the top-left cell; the line break after the last row ends the text.
A range that holds the values a whole number of times is filled with them.
Three rows do not hold two values a whole number of times: they are pasted once.
Rows are never added.
Read-only cells are not skipped: they refuse the paste.
Without values, paste does nothing.
The first row goes into the others; (2, region) already holds Tokyo.
A range of one row takes the row above it.
A value goes into a column of another type through its text form.
A range of one column takes the column left of it.
undo writes the values before, each with previous set to the values after.
Steps name cells by key, so they are written whatever the view.
